curl_direct_no_proxy.note: the JS layout, as expected for a modern UA -- the same egress is not /sorry-walled as such

summary: /wml with a legacy UA answers 302 -> /sorry from every egress reachable from this host: 0/17 across the home IP, DE/GB/US residential exits, six whitelisted UAs, and both our browser engines. The route the legacy_wap device was shipped for (#130) is closed as of this date; whether Google closed it for everyone or flagged every egress we own cannot be told apart from here, but three residential countries plus the home IP all at 0 makes the former the parsimonious reading. The JS /search path from the same egresses still returns a SERP to curl. Addendum: SearXNG's current recipe -- the same Nokia UA over curl_cffi impersonate='chrome99_android', the fix its maintainer named for Google's TLS inspection on 2026-08-23 -- is 0/6 from here too (direct 0/2, DE/GB exits 0/4). So TLS impersonation does not reopen the route from any egress this host reaches; whether it still works from other egress classes is undetermined. Addendum 2: carrier-ASN exits (GB Three = AS206067 Hutchison 3G UK, US AT&T = AS7018) refuse it just the same, over plain TLS, chrome99_android and the browser path (0/7). Nothing this account can reach opens /wml.

curl_cffi_impersonate_chrome99_android.why: SearXNG's google engine (searx/engines/google.py at master, 2026-09-17) still sends a Nokia UA to /wml/search but sets impersonate='chrome99_android' per request; its maintainer wrote on 2026-08-23 (issue #6570) that Google 'are doing TLS inspection now' and that curl_cffi impersonation made the Nokia UA work again; the network layer migrated to curl_cffi on 2026-09-03 (PR #6620). This is that exact recipe, run from the worker image with curl_cffi 0.16.3; script: research/wml_refused_2026_09_17_impersonate.py.

carrier_asn_exits.why: The maintainer's hypothesis: a 2004 feature phone is plausible only from a carrier network, so the residential/home egresses were the tell. The account has no LTE category (proxy_type=mobile/mobile_shared -> no_more_proxies, category=lte, total=0 in DE/GB/US/RU), but the premium v2 pool lists carrier ISPs (GB 'Three', 'Vodafone UK'; US 'AT&T Wireless', 'Verizon'; DE 'O2 Deutschland', 'Vodafone Germany', 'Deutsche Telekom AG'), reachable through prem_proxy_options.isp. The exit's ASN org was read via ipinfo (address never recorded).
carrier_asn_exits.verdict: A genuine mobile-carrier ASN (Hutchison 3G UK, i.e. Three's mobile network) changes nothing: 0/4 with the Nokia UA over both TLS shapes, and 0/3 through the browser path. The carrier hypothesis is measured and closed, with the caveat that an ISP-targeted residential pool exit on a carrier's AS is not proof of a handset-class IP.
